subject: Day 32: enroll in Music Together
bodyText:
Today's focus
Avi is 32 days old. This is capacity-planning week for enrichment: top Bay Area parent-baby music terms fill on waitlists, so securing a slot now sets the year-2 trajectory. The class itself starts later, but the booking is the time-sensitive move.

Action items
- Enroll in or waitlist a Music Together term for the next eligible session; classes accept infants from about six weeks, and prime time slots carry multi-month waitlists in SF and the East Bay. Music Together: https://www.musictogether.com/
- Increase cumulative tummy time toward 20 to 30 minutes a day across short bouts now that Avi sustains 10 to 20 second head lifts. AAP HealthyChildren: Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Keep daycare tours or nanny interviews active if return to work lands in seven to eleven weeks; nanny searches take four to eight weeks and top daycares run long waitlists.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cradle cap (yellow scale on the scalp) and a blocked tear duct (continuous tearing in one eye with no redness); both are common and self-limited at this age.
- [monitor] Crying that clusters in the evening witching hour from roughly 5 to 8pm; track duration so you can distinguish a normal pattern from the Wessel colic threshold.
- [call within 24h] Sustained refusal of multiple feeds in a row, or forceful painful spit-up paired with arching that disrupts feeding.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, blue color around the lips with crying, labored breathing, or seizure-like activity; for blue lips, call 911 immediately!

Enrichment opportunities
- Enroll or waitlist a Music Together or Kindermusik term; the highest-evidence music intervention is live participatory class, and securing the slot early protects the start date. Music Together: https://www.musictogether.com/
- Set up mirror tummy time: prop a baby-safe mirror at his eye level so face-tracking motivates the head lifts; the mirror is the single strongest motivator for prone tolerance. AAP HealthyChildren: Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Read aloud for 15 minutes with rhythmic, repetitive text so the beat of the words carries the session; shared book time in infancy is foundational for later language and reading. AAP Early Literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/

Upcoming
- Day 35-41 (around week 6): Anoushka's 6-week postpartum visit; expect exercise clearance for an uncomplicated delivery plus a final mood screen.
- Day 56-70 (2-month well visit): vaccines are HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1.
- Day 57-72 (post-vaccine window): anticipate fussiness and low-grade fever for a day or two after.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete
